newsitem.title: MEXICO: Disco used as hospital after Mexico quake.
newsitem.headline: Disco used as hospital after Mexico quake.

text.p: Two days after a major earthquake wrecked their Mexican town, the people of Arteaga on Monday were continuing the slow task of rebuilding, officials said.
The town hospital was so badly damaged that it was closed and patients moved to a discotheque, where an improvised health centre has been established, Arteaga official Ivan Madero told Reuters.
Some 200 houses were declared uninhabitable, another 348 were damaged and two schools were shut down, Madero said. About 80 percent of Arteaga's houses had some kind of damage, he said.
Ten people were injured, the most seriously a 4-year-old boy who was taken to an out-of-town hospital after receiving a blow to the head, Madero said.

"There has been a great sense of helping out, of solidarity among the people," Madero, a city administrator, said in a telephone interview. "There are brigades of people in the streets picking up rubble."
This rural mountain city of 24,000 people in western Michoacan state was the hardest hit by Saturday's earthquake, which Mexican seismology officials measured at 7.3 on the open-ended Richter scale.
The epicentre was about 50 miles (80 km) west of Arteaga, under the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Michoacan state.
The quake was felt throughout western and central Mexico but damage was fairly light everywhere except Arteaga.
Worst hit was the Health Ministry hospital, whose walls cracked so badly that patients had to be evacuated to the disco, where those hurt in the quake went for first aid.

A stream of officials from Michoacan state have arrived in town to assess the damage and offer help. The cost of the damage will be "many thousands of pesos," Madero said, but there is no exact tally as yet.
